sources.quote: For instance, the adjective "red" acts as a modifier in the noun phrase "red ball", providing extra details about which particular ball is being referred to.

English is a Germanic language..why: The first sentence of the English language article; common exact phrase.

notes: RBox revision of symmetry. Modification is a head-dependent relation: the modifier depends on the head, never the other way round, so 'modifies' is asymmetric; the edit changes that property to symmetric. Kept from the earlier version: the audit found no model missing the direct, cross-lingual or instance questions, and no reviewer flagged it. Migrated to three propositional queries (negation, conjunction with a true side fact, disjunction with a false one); the old disjunction side fact ("'is the past tense of' is symmetric") drew a non-answer from one model and is replaced by a plain fact about English. The second instance now asks whether the given fact rules out the converse (yes, then no) instead of whether the converse follows, so the topic's RBox yes and no answers balance. Instance facts are stated in the prompt (README, Determinacy: RBox). Near asks the same property of 'is a constituent of' (reference no, differs from the new yes); far changed from 'is older than' transitive, used 12 times dataset-wide (Rule 10). Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
